mn17:1.2: On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Savatthi, in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park.
mn17:1.3: There he addressed the bhikkhus thus:
mn17:2.1: ‘Bhikkhus, I shall expound to you a discourse on jungle thickets.
mn17:2.2: Listen and heed well what I shall say.’
mn17:2.3: ‘Even so, venerable sir’, the bhikkhus replied.
mn17:3.1: ‘Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu lives in some jungle thicket.
mn17:3.2: While living there his unestablished mindfulness does not become established, his unconcentrated mind does not become concentrated, his unexhausted taints do not come to exhaustion, the unattained supreme surcease of bondage is not attained;
mn17:3.3: and also the requisites for the life of one gone forth that should be available—robes, alms-food, resting place and the requisite of medicine as cure for the sick—are hard to come by.
mn17:3.4: The bhikkhu should take count of this.
mn17:3.7: He should depart from that jungle thicket that very night or that very day; he should not continue living there.
mn17:4.1: ‘Here a bhikkhu lives in some jungle thicket.
mn17:4.2: While living there his unestablished mindfulness does not become established, his unconcentrated mind does not become concentrated, his unexhausted taints do not come to exhaustion, the unattained supreme surcease of bondage is not attained;
mn17:4.3: yet the requisites for the life of one gone forth that should be available—robes, alms-food, resting place and the requisite of medicine as cure for the sick—are easy to come by.
mn17:4.4: The bhikkhu should take count of this, but he should reflect thus:
mn17:4.7: “I did not go forth from the home life into homelessness for the sake of robes, alms-food, resting place and the requisite of medcine as cure for the sick;
mn17:4.8: but yet I make no progress here.”
mn17:4.9: He should depart from that jungle thicket after weighing the matter; he should not continue living there.
mn17:5.1: ‘Here a bhikkhu lives in some jungle thicket.
mn17:5.2: While living there his unestablished mindfulness becomes established, his unconcentrated mind becomes concentrated, his unexhausted taints come to exhaustion, the unattained supreme surcease of bondage is attained;
mn17:5.3: yet the requisites for the life of one gone forth that should be available—robes, alms-food, resting place and the requisite of medicine as cure for the sick—are hard to come by. The bhikkhu should take count of this, but should reflect thus:
mn17:5.7: “I did not go forth from home life into homelessness for the sake of robes, alms-food, resting place, and the requisite of medicine as cure for the sick;
mn17:5.8: but yet I make progress here.”
mn17:5.9: He should continue living in that jungle thicket after weighing the matter; he should not depart.
mn17:6.1: ‘Here a bhikkhu lives in some jungle thicket.
mn17:6.2: While living there his unestablished mindfulness becomes established, his unconcentrated mind becomes concentrated, his unexhausted taints come to exhaustion, the unattained supreme surcease of bondage is attained;
mn17:6.3: and also the requisites for the life of one gone forth that should be available—robes, alms-food, resting place, and the requisite of medicine as cure for the sick—are easy to come by.
mn17:6.4: The bhikkhu should take count of this.
mn17:6.7: He should continue living in that jungle thicket as long as life lasts; he should not depart.

mn17:26.1: ‘Here a bhikkhu lives with a certain person …
mn17:26.2: While living there his unestablished mindfulness becomes established, his unconcentrated mind becomes concentrated, his unexhausted taints come to exhaustion, the unattained supreme surcease of bondage is attained;
mn17:26.3: and also the requisites for the life of one gone forth that should be available—robes, alms-food, resting place, and the requisite of medicine as cure for the sick—are easy to come by.
mn17:26.7: He should continue following that person as long as life lasts; he should not depart from him even if told to go.’
mn17:26.8: That is what the Blessed One said.
mn17:26.9: The bhikkhus were satisfied, and they delighted in the Blessed One’s words.
